rulings.Case Title: CONSERVATORSHIP OF JUANITA WALKER
rulings.Calendar Matter: ACCOUNTING PETITION RE: Accounting #1, Report, Fees
rulings.Rulings: Continued to 9/9/26. (No earlier availability.) Issue(s) necessitating continuance: (1) No proposed order has been lodged or received by the assigned examiner. [LRSF 14.7 A. and 14.59 E.] (2) No proof of service of notice of this hearing has been filed. (3) Notice must have attached to it the procedures for how to make a remote appearance by Zoom and CourtCall, as well as remote public access, as set out at https://sf.courts.ca.gov/divisions/probate-court. [LRSF 14.1 C.6.] (4) Original financial institution statements do not appear to have been filed. [Probate Code Section 2620(c)(2).] (5) A final accounting following the death of a conservatee shall include an accounting for the period that ended on the date of death and a separate accounting for the period subsequent to the date of death. [Probate Code Section 2620(b).] Please provide a proposed order and courtesy copies of the petition and any papers filed to address these issues to the assigned examiner by 8/26/26. The petition has not been fully reviewed, as no courtesy copy was provided, as required by LRSF 2.7 B. and 14.7 B.; however, a cursory glance at the pleading online shows a different starting amount for the cash from the amount reported on the I&A filed on 6/23/25, the prayer does not appear to include any of the amounts Conservator is requesting to disburse, and the prayer requests distribution to a purported "sole heir," effectively bypassing probate - without any authority. Examiner continuances are final and not subject to contest under LRSF 14.10 B.

rulings.Rulings: Continued to 08/24/2026 (no earlier date available). 1) Proof of service attached to the DE-120 form on file shows that notice was given on 06/10/2026, less than 30 days before this hearing. New notice must be given. 2) Notice must be given to the settlor-conservatee. As the conservatee's court-appointed attorney's scope of representation has not been expanded to include this trust matter, the attorney has no authority to waive notice on behalf of the settlor under Probate Code section 1204. 3) The governing trust does not authorize each co-trustee to act independently and bind the trust without the other co-trustee's consent, as requested by the amendment. No petition for substituted judgment has been filed in the related conservatorship case for modification of the conservatee's revocable trust as a proposed action. 4) A copy of the proposed order must be served on each person entitled to notice, if this matter becomes contested. rulings.Case Title: THE ESTATE OF LORNA LIGUID PALANCA
rulings.Calendar Matter: PETITION FOR LETTERS OF ADMINISTRATION
rulings.Rulings: Continued to 7/29/2026. The following issues must be cleared two weeks prior to the hearing: (1) Petitioners' supplement states that neither Petition #7(1) nor (2) applies because her brother left less than $10K. This allegation appears to indicate that no part of the decedent's estate is attributable to the predeceased spouse. In such circumstances, the petitioners may not have priority of appointment under PrC sec. 8461(n), as the requirements of Sec. 8462(a) are not met. Therefore, the San Francisco Public Administrator, who holds higher priority under Sec. 8461(p), must receive proper notice. (2) The petition does not identify the decedent's heirs at law. All heirs must be listed in Petition #8 and properly notified. If petitioners do not know of any relatives or heirs, they must file a declaration of diligent search. The court will review these efforts and decide if an heir search company is needed. (3) Petition #8 must indicate the date of death of all deceased heirs, including the decedent's parents.
